hints.title: Odd Frequency Parity Restriction
hints.text: A string can be rearranged into a palindrome if and only if at most one character appears an odd number of times.

hints.title: Character Frequency Counting
hints.text: Count frequencies of every distinct character. Verify that the number of characters with odd occurrences does not exceed one.

hints.title: Bitwise or Frequency Map Verification
hints.text: Count character occurrences across the string. Sum the number of entries with odd count; return true if odd count is zero or one, otherwise return false.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def canPermutePalindrome(self, s: str) -> bool:
        from collections import Counter
        counts = Counter(s)
        odd_count = sum(1 for c in counts.values() if c % 2 == 1)
        return odd_count <= 1
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all string permutations takes factorial O(N!) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting character frequencies takes linear time and bounded O(1) space since character set is small.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should directly state the necessary and sufficient condition: at most one odd-frequency character.
